tasks.instruction: Swap the two 4-bit groups of the lowest byte of the input and leave every bit above the lowest byte unchanged.
tasks.note: Start shifts by 3 instead of 4. Wrongs drop the upper bits, or mask 8 bits before shifting left.

tasks.instruction: Return a value with only the lowest set bit of the input kept (zero when the input is zero).
tasks.note: Start clears the lowest set bit instead; the fix relies on 0 minus the input wrapping.

tasks.instruction: Return true only when the days elapsed (first input) are strictly more than the grace days (second input) and the amount owed (third input) is not zero.
tasks.note: Start treats the last grace day as late.

tasks.instruction: Return true when at least two of the three boolean inputs are true.
tasks.note: Start ignores the pair of second and third inputs; the wrong edit pairs the second and third inputs with xor, which fails when only those two are true.

tasks.instruction: Return an array whose element k is the wrapping sum of input elements 0 through k.
tasks.note: Start's third sum omits the first element.

tasks.instruction: Return the wrapping difference first minus second, paired with a flag that is true exactly when the subtraction borrowed (second input larger than the first).
tasks.note: Start has the comparison reversed. Record results are written as JSON arrays [field0, field1].

tasks.instruction: Count, for each value 0 to 3, how many of the four input elements have that value in their lowest two bits; every element must be counted exactly once.
tasks.note: Start stops one element early; a count of 5 wraps around and counts the first element twice.

tasks.instruction: Return the wrapping total of the four elements together with a flag that is true only when the total is strictly greater than the budget (second input).
tasks.note: Start flags a total equal to the budget. Record results are written as JSON arrays.

tasks.instruction: Units up to and including 10 cost 5 each; every unit beyond the tenth costs 3, so the price above 10 units is 50 plus 3 per extra unit (wrapping).
Pack three channels into one value as first<<16 | second<<8 | third, using only the low 8 bits of each input so that oversized inputs cannot spill into neighbouring channels.
Swap elements 0 and 1 and also swap elements 2 and 3, returning the new array.
tasks.note: Start swaps only the first pair; the wrong edit writes the same value into both slots.

tasks.instruction: Apply the existing scale helper to both inputs and return the scaled first input minus the scaled second input (wrapping).
tasks.note: Start adds the raw second input.

tasks.instruction: The checksum must start from 17 instead of 7, and every step must also add the element's position to the running value.
tasks.note: Start uses the old seed and no position mixing; the edit touches both functions.

tasks.instruction: Return how many bits are needed to write the input in binary: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 2 for 2 and 3, up to 32 for values with the top bit set.
tasks.note: Start returns the index of the highest set bit; the greater-than-1 wrong is off by one; fold count 31 misses the top bit.

tasks.instruction: Count the neighbouring positions (0,1), (1,2) and (2,3) whose elements are equal; the last element must not be compared with the first.
tasks.note: Start's fold also compares element 3 with element 0 because the index wraps.

tasks.instruction: Return true only when every element is strictly smaller than the next one; equal neighbours make the result false.
tasks.note: Start accepts equal neighbours; the edit is in the step helper.
